english: present Konjunktiv I — formed from the verb stem, not the Präsens
note: kommen → ich komme, du kommest, er komme, wir kommen, ihr kommet, sie kommen. Built from the infinitive stem, so it never has an umlaut change or irregular vowel shift.

examples.de: Er sagte, er komme später.
examples.en: He said he was coming later.

german: sein im Konjunktiv I (sei, seist, sei, seien, seiet, seien)
english: "sein" in Konjunktiv I — the form you'll use constantly
note: irregular, and by far the most common Konjunktiv I verb in reported speech: "er sei", "sie seien". Learn this one by heart.

examples.de: Sie sagte, sie sei krank.
examples.en: She said she was sick.

english: "haben" in Konjunktiv I — the auxiliary for the reported past
note: ich habe, du habest, er habe, wir haben, ihr habet, sie haben. "er habe" is the everyday one, used to build the reported past.

examples.de: Er sagte, er habe keine Zeit gehabt.
examples.en: He said he'd had no time.

english: "werden" in Konjunktiv I — for reported claims about the future
note: ich werde, du werdest, er werde, wir werden, ihr werdet, sie werden. Reports a promise or prediction someone made.

examples.de: Der Minister sagte, die Regierung werde das Gesetz unterstützen.
examples.en: The minister said the government would support the law.

german: er/sie/es + Konjunktiv I (er komme, sie sei)
english: the 3rd person singular — the clearest, most useful Konjunktiv I form
note: "er komme" ≠ "er kommt" (indicative), so this form is never confusable — it's the one you can trust and reuse most.

examples.de: Der Sprecher erklärte, die Lage sei unter Kontrolle.
examples.en: The spokesperson explained that the situation was under control.

english: the 2nd person singular — also clearly distinct, but rare (direct address is rarely reported)
note: grammatically distinct from the indicative, but you'll mostly meet it in older or very formal writing — 3rd person dominates real reported speech.

examples.de: Er fragte, ob du kommest.
examples.en: He asked whether you were coming.

german: Ersatzform: Konjunktiv II, wenn Konjunktiv I = Indikativ
english: when Konjunktiv I looks identical to the indicative, use Konjunktiv II instead
note: the single most important rule here. ich/wir/sie(Plural)-forms of Konjunktiv I usually collide with the indicative, so German swaps in Konjunktiv II to keep the "this is reported" signal clear.

examples.de: Sie sagten, sie kämen später. (nicht: sie kommen, da identisch mit dem Indikativ)
examples.en: They said they were coming later.

english: "they were coming" — Konjunktiv II standing in for a collided Konjunktiv I
note: "sie kommen" as Konjunktiv I is identical to the indicative, so "sie kämen" (Konjunktiv II) is used to report it instead.

examples.de: Die Nachbarn erzählten, sie hätten den Termin verschoben.
examples.en: The neighbours said they had postponed the appointment.

english: reported speech with a dass-clause (verb to the end)
note: "Er sagte, dass er müde sei." The most explicit, unambiguous option — and the easiest to build correctly.

examples.de: Sie erklärte, dass sie den Termin nicht einhalten könne.
examples.en: She explained that she couldn't keep the appointment.

german: indirekte Rede ohne dass (Verb an Position 2)
english: reported speech without dass — normal verb-second word order
note: same meaning, more formal/journalistic: "Er sagte, er sei müde." No comma-triggered verb-final — it's its own main-clause-shaped sentence.

examples.de: Der Zeuge sagte, er habe nichts gesehen.
examples.en: The witness said he had seen nothing.

german: Vergangenheit in der indirekten Rede: habe/sei + Partizip II
english: one past form covers every original past tense
note: whether the original was Präteritum, Perfekt, or Plusquamperfekt, reported speech uses just ONE past form: habe/sei (Konjunktiv I) + Partizip II.

examples.de: "Ich war krank." → Er sagte, er sei krank gewesen.
examples.en: "I was sick." → He said he had been sick.

german: Er sagte, er sei müde gewesen.
english: "He said he had been tired." — a worked past-tense example
note: sei (Konjunktiv I of sein) + gewesen (Partizip II) — reports "Ich war müde" regardless of whether the original was Präteritum or Perfekt.

examples.de: "Wir haben lange gewartet." → Sie sagten, sie hätten lange gewartet.
examples.en: "We waited a long time." → They said they had waited a long time.

english: a reported yes/no question, introduced with "ob"
note: "Kommst du?" → "Sie fragte, ob ich käme." Verb to the end, same tense logic as any other reported clause.

examples.de: Er fragte, ob sie den Vertrag schon unterschrieben habe.
examples.en: He asked whether she had already signed the contract.

english: a reported question with a question word — the word word stays, verb moves to the end
note: "Wann kommst du?" → "Er fragte, wann ich käme." The W-word (wann, wo, warum, wie …) does the job "ob" does for yes/no questions.

examples.de: Sie wollte wissen, warum der Zug Verspätung habe.
examples.en: She wanted to know why the train was late.

english: a reported command or request — sollen or mögen + Infinitiv
note: "Mach das!" → "Er sagte, ich solle das machen." "möge" is more formal/polite ("Man möge verstehen, dass …").

examples.de: Die Chefin sagte, wir sollten pünktlich sein.
examples.en: The boss said we should be punctual.

german: Konjunktiv I ist vor allem Schriftsprache
english: Konjunktiv I lives mainly in writing — especially news
note: in everyday speech, people mostly just use "dass" + indicative, or the subjective modals from Unit 8 (soll, will). Konjunktiv I is more a reading skill than a speaking one.

examples.de: In den Nachrichten heißt es, die Zahlen seien gestiegen.
examples.en: The news says the figures have risen.

english: signalling that the speaker isn't vouching for the claim
note: Konjunktiv I marks "this is what was said, I'm not confirming it" — the same job "soll"/"will" do (Unit 8), just in writing rather than speech.

examples.de: Der Angeklagte sei zur Tatzeit nicht am Ort gewesen, so sein Anwalt.
examples.en: The defendant was not at the scene at the time, according to his lawyer.

english: to report
note: "berichten, dass …" / "über etwas berichten". The standard reporting verb for news.

examples.de: Die Zeitung berichtete, die Firma habe Verluste gemacht.
examples.en: The newspaper reported that the company had made losses.

english: to explain, state, declare
note: "erklären, dass …". Also "sich bereit erklären, … zu …" = to declare oneself willing to.

examples.de: Der Sprecher erklärte, man werde die Preise nicht erhöhen.
examples.en: The spokesperson stated that prices would not be raised.

english: to emphasise, stress
note: "betonen, dass …" — marks that the speaker wanted this point especially noticed.

examples.de: Sie betonte, dass ihr die Sicherheit besonders wichtig sei.
examples.en: She stressed that safety was especially important to her.

english: to add (a further remark)
note: separable: fügt … hinzu. Common at the end of a reported-speech paragraph: "Er fügte hinzu, dass …".

examples.de: Sie fügte hinzu, das Ergebnis überrasche sie nicht.
examples.en: She added that the result didn't surprise her.

english: to think, be of the opinion, mean
note: softer than "behaupten" (Unit 8) — a stated opinion, not necessarily doubted: "Er meinte, das sei keine gute Idee."

examples.de: Viele meinen, die Regeln seien zu streng.
examples.en: Many think the rules are too strict.

english: to inform, communicate (formally)
note: separable, official register: "Das Amt teilte mit, der Antrag sei genehmigt worden."

examples.de: Die Bahn teilte mit, der Zug falle aus.
examples.en: The railway announced that the train would be cancelled.

english: to comment (on), express an opinion
note: reflexive; "sich zu etwas äußern" = to comment on something. "Die Firma wollte sich dazu nicht äußern" = the company declined to comment.

examples.de: Der Politiker äußerte sich nicht zu den Vorwürfen.
examples.en: The politician did not comment on the allegations.

english: quotation
note: "jemanden zitieren" = to quote someone (direct speech); reported speech is the alternative when you paraphrase instead.

examples.de: Das Zitat stammt aus einem Interview von letzter Woche.
examples.en: The quotation comes from an interview from last week.

english: direct speech — the exact original words
note: in quotation marks, unchanged: "Ich bin müde", sagte er. Contrast with die indirekte Rede.

examples.de: In wörtlicher Rede steht der Originalwortlaut in Anführungszeichen.
examples.en: In direct speech, the original wording stands in quotation marks.

english: indirect / reported speech
note: paraphrasing what someone said, usually in Konjunktiv I (or its Konjunktiv II substitute). No quotation marks.

examples.de: In der indirekten Rede ändert sich oft die Perspektive der Pronomen.
examples.en: In indirect speech, the perspective of the pronouns often changes.

english: news language / journalese
note: the register where Konjunktiv I is genuinely common — radio and print news reporting what officials, witnesses, or spokespeople said.

examples.de: Typisch für die Nachrichtensprache ist der häufige Konjunktiv I.
examples.en: Frequent use of Konjunktiv I is typical of news language.
